title: Platform worker injuries and work injury compensation
asked: Whether the Ministry of Manpower plans more measures to further cut fatal and major injuries among platform workers, and to strengthen financial protection for work injury, given their relatively high injury rate.
response: MOM has convened a Platform Worker Safety Workgroup with Government agencies, platform operators, NTUC and platform work associations. Since 1 January 2025, platform workers get work injury compensation at the same coverage level as employees, covering medical expenses, income loss for medical and hospitalisation leave, and lump sums for permanent incapacity or death. MOM regularly reviews compensation limits under the Work Injury Compensation Act; changes effective 1 November 2025 raised maximum coverage to $53,000 for medical expenses, $346,000 for permanent incapacity and $269,000 for death.

key_points.point: A Platform Worker Safety Workgroup has been set up with Government agencies, platform operators, NTUC and platform work associations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash

key_points.point: The workgroup is looking at detection of unsafe behaviours and at encouraging positive safety behaviours rather than relying only on compensation or punitive measures.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash

key_points.point: Safety awareness and education efforts include how platform workers move around areas with civilians, residents and traffic, especially those on two-wheeled devices and bicycles.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: particularly focused on our platform workers who may be operating off two-wheeled devices and bicycles

left_open: Whether any interim measures are needed while the workgroup develops longer-term solutions.
supplementary: Whether interim measures are needed while the workgroup works out longer-term solutions, and how detection, awareness and safety education can be improved.
